excerpts:
# Claude Sonnet 5.5
**Performance.** Sonnet 5.5 scores 70.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, an agentic coding evaluation, compared to Sonnet 5’s 10.3%. It scores two points below Opus 5.5 on GDPval-AA, a test of real-world work across a variety of occupations. And it’s strong on long-horizon work and image understanding—it’s the first Sonnet model to beat _Pokémon Red_ working only from screenshots.
**Cost.** Sonnet 5.5 is priced the same as Sonnet 5 at $2 per million input tokens, $10 per million output tokens, and $0.20 per million tokens for cache reads, but it typically needs far fewer tokens to do the same work. In our testing, it costs up to 30% less per task than its predecessor.

## Performance
Sonnet 5.5 improves on Sonnet 5 across domains—in some cases dramatically. On several evaluations, Sonnet 5.5 at Max effort even performs comparably to Opus 5.5. However, benchmark scores capture only one facet of a model’s capabilities; in our own testing, and in that of external testers, Opus 5.5 remains clearly stronger at complex, open-ended work requiring sustained judgment.

results.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Pricing vs Opus 5.5: Is Cheaper Actually Cheaper? | MindStudio
excerpts:
* **Per-token pricing** still favors Sonnet 5.5 over Opus 5.5, but that gap shrinks or disappears once you measure cost per completed task instead of cost per million tokens.
* **Max effort mode** on Sonnet 5.5 generates significantly more reasoning tokens to hit benchmark-topping scores, and those extra tokens are what get billed.

...

* **Cost-per-task benchmarks** , like the ones tracked on aggregators such as Artificial Analysis, showed both Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 landing in a similarly expensive range, roughly $6 to $8 per task, far above cheaper competitors.
* **GPT 6.1 Soul** , announced the same week at OpenAI’s dev day, undercuts both Anthropic models dramatically on cost per task, landing around 72 cents, while trailing them by only a few points on blended intelligence benchmarks.

# Claude Sonnet 5.5 Pricing vs Opus 5.5: Is Cheaper Actually Cheaper?
## Why does Sonnet’s advertised price not match real-world cost?
Opus 5.5 is Anthropic’s top-end model. It doesn’t need extended reasoning effort cranked to maximum to post strong numbers; its baseline is already tuned for capability. Sonnet 5.5, to close the gap with Opus on hard benchmarks, often needs to run in its highest reasoning or “max effort” configuration.

...

## What did the benchmark data actually show?
Looking at blended intelligence-versus-cost tracking from aggregator sites like Artificial Analysis, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 both clustered in the same expensive territory on a cost-per-task basis, somewhere around $6 to $8 per task. That’s a strange result if you only looked at headline per-token pricing and assumed Sonnet would be meaningfully cheaper to run.

...

Soul’s list price is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, compared to Astra’s $10 input and $50 output.
The pattern across nearly every benchmark mentioned was consistent: the more expensive model scored a bit higher, and the cheaper model landed close behind at a fraction of the cost per completed task. Sonnet 5.5 broke that pattern when pushed to max effort, costing Opus-level money without delivering an Opus-level jump in score.

## Frequently Asked Questions
### How does GPT 6.1 Soul compare to Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 on price?
GPT 6.1 Soul is priced at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, well below Opus 5.5 and Astra’s rates, and its cost per task on blended benchmarks came in far lower too, around 72 cents versus roughly $6 to $8 for Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 at max effort.

# Claude Sonnet 5.5 Released: Benchmarks, Pricing, vs Opus 5.5
## Where Claude Sonnet 5.5 is available
It shipped everywhere on day one. On the Claude API it is `claude-sonnet-5-5` for all customers. Amazon Bedrock serves it through the global cross-region profile `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5` , and Claude Platform on AWS (North America at launch) uses the plain ID. Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry both use `claude-sonnet-5-5` . Zero data retention is available, as with Opus 5.5.
In the tools developers use daily, Claude Code picked it up the same day as the default Sonnet on the Anthropic API, at medium effort. GitHub Copilot made it generally available to Pro, Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise with a gradual rollout, and Cursor lists it in the model picker under Settings, Models.

## Which effort level to run Sonnet 5.5 at
Start at medium. In our runs it was the only setting that was cheap, fast and correct at once: Sonnet 5’s token bill, faster than Sonnet 5, and every manifest deployed. It is also what Claude Code already uses, so in the terminal you get the good setting without touching anything.
On the API, set `output_config.effort` explicitly, because the default of high roughly doubled output tokens on routine generation with no gain we could measure. Move to high or xhigh for long, open-ended agentic work, where Anthropic’s CursorBench series shows real gains.
Keep max for evals that prove it pays: on FrontierCode it scored below xhigh, and on our tasks it bought identical results for twenty times the money.

# Claude Sonnet 4.6
## Availability and pricing
Anyone can chat with Claude using Sonnet 5.5 on Claude.ai, available on web, iOS, and Android.
For developers interested in building agents, Sonnet 5.5 is available on the Claude Platform natively, and in Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry.
Pricing for Sonnet 5.5 will cost up to an estimated 30% less to run than Sonnet 5 for typical workloads billed by token.
Sonnet 5.5 is priced at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with up to 90% cost savings with [prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching) and 50% cost savings with [batch processing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing) . To learn more, check out our [pricing page](https://claude.com/pricing) .
To get started, simply use `claude-sonnet-5-5` via the [Claude API](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview) .
For workloads that need to run in the US, US-only inference is available at 1.1x pricing for input and output tokens. [Learn more](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/data-residency) .

## Use cases
Sonnet 5.5 is a faster, lower-cost complement to Opus 5.5. It excels at well-scoped everyday tasks across coding, agents, and knowledge work.

Claude Sonnet 5.5, released September 28, 2026, was the second model of Anthropic's 5.5 generation, six days after Claude Opus 5.5 and three months after Claude Sonnet 5 opened the 5-series at the mid tier.
The price stayed at Sonnet 5's $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output, with cache reads at $0.20, but Anthropic said the model needed far fewer tokens for the same work, for up to 30% lower cost per task, and generated output more than 30% faster, which made it the fastest Sonnet at the time.
At launch it was available through Anthropic's API as claude-sonnet-5-5 and on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry, with Claude Haiku 5.5 announced to follow in the coming weeks.
When was Claude Sonnet 5.5 released? Claude Sonnet 5.5 was released by Anthropic on Monday, Sep 28 2026.
Who made Claude Sonnet 5.5? Claude Sonnet 5.5 was built by Anthropic. AI safety company building the Claude family of models. Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers.
How much does Claude Sonnet 5.5 cost?
Claude Sonnet 5.5 costs $2.00 per million input tokens and $10.00 per million output tokens through the Anthropic API. Cached input is $0.20 per million tokens. Rates are pay-as-you-go API prices verified against Anthropic's published pricing on September 28, 2026.
What benchmark scores did Claude Sonnet 5.5 get?
Claude Sonnet 5.5 reports 8 tracked benchmark scores — BullshitBench v2: 60%; CursorBench 4.0: 55.5%; FrontierCode v1.1 (Main) (main split): 52.1%; Terminal-Bench 4.0: 70.6%; Humanity's Last Exam (with tools): 64.5%; GDPval-AA v2.1: 1844; AA-Briefcase v1.1: 1811; Chartography (no tools): 61.6%.
Tracked scores may come from lab reports or independent benchmarks; source details accompany the benchmark data. It holds the best score among all models tracked here on Terminal-Bench 4.0.
What is the context window of Claude Sonnet 5.5? Claude Sonnet 5.5 has a context window of 1M.
